Implementation, migration, UAT and adoption

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Plan a tenant implementation
  • Reconcile migration exactly
  • Separate sandbox readiness from production admission

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Discovery + scope
  2. 02Configuration + mapping
  3. 03Dry run + reconciliation
  4. 04UAT + training
  5. 05Four-eyes cutover
  6. 06Hypercare + admission evidence

1. Controlled implementation

Discovery maps products, processes, roles, data, integrations, controls and gaps into versioned configuration and accountable work.

Product administration exposes server-versioned forms, repeatable staffing, lifecycle history, diffs, evidence references and blockers; those references still require authoritative joins.

Scope changes reopen affected evidence.

2. Migration

Mapping packs, cleansed source extracts, dry runs, rejects, exact financial reconciliation, cutover and rollback are tenant scoped and independently approved. Unreconciled balances block launch.

3. Adoption and admission

Role training, sandbox campaigns, UAT, operating procedures, staffing, support and witnessed cutover join technical evidence. Simulator success can establish sandbox readiness, never live production readiness.
